subject: additive and dominance effects in a binary model

messages.author: b851f9a8b81a6867
messages.subject: additive and dominance effects in a binary model
parts:
Hi Dr Karl

I detected a QTL using binary model (my phenotypes were either 0 or 1) and got the following results using fitqtl. I am having a hard time interpreting the estimates of additive effects.
I think by definition additive effects are supposed to be the effect of substituting one allele to the other. So I would have expected the additive effect to be around 0.4 or -0.4. Can you please help me interpret the following results.

I am also not sure why the degrees of freedom is 2 in this case. I agree that percent phenotypic variance explained by the locus was ~63%, after I used the formula and confirmed that was indeed correct.


 fitqtl summary

Method: Haley-Knott regression 
Model:  binary phenotype
Number of observations : 269 

Full model result
----------------------------------  
Model formula: y ~ Q1 

      df      LOD     %var Pvalue(Chi2)
Model  2 57.96588 62.92963            0


Estimated effects:
-----------------
              est      SE      t
Intercept  3.8758  0.7188  5.392
8...@140.0a  -3.7793  0.6263 -6.034
8...@140.0d   7.2236  1.8111  3.988

Thanks a lot for your help in advance
Raghu

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] additive and dominance effects in a binary model
parts:
With the binary phenotype, we're fitting a logistic regression model, so the estimated effects concern log odds.

karl
